author: Temminck, 1836
summary: 우리나라에 해마다 수만 마리가 찾아와 번식하는 여름철새로, 바다에서 무리를 지어 지내며 울릉도와 제주도에서 관찰된다. 날개가 길어 제자리에서 바로 날아오르지 못하고, 나무나 벼랑 위에서 뛰어내리거나 달려가다가 떠오른다. 땅속에 굴을 파서 둥지를 만들고 6~7월에 흰 알 1개를 낳아 암수가 번갈아 품는다. 물고기, 오징어, 낙지, 해조류 등을 먹으며, 국외에서는 중국 해안에 분포한다.

art.subject: Streaked Shearwater (Calonectris leucomelas), adult in the breeding season, as seen at sea off Korean islands in summer: forehead, crown and nape white, densely streaked blackish-brown; face whiter with fine streaks; hindneck and sides of the neck brown; upperparts dark grey-brown, the back and uppertail-covert feathers fringed pale, giving a scaly look; upperwing dark brown; underparts clean white; underwing coverts white, bordered by dark flight feathers; tail dark brown. Long, slender, pale pinkish-horn bill with tube nostrils and a darker hooked tip; dark eye; pinkish legs and feet.
art.pose: gliding low over the waves on long wings
art.scene: Korean summer sea off a steep island coast such as Ulleungdo; no people, buildings or text
views: adult in flight seen from above: dark grey-brown upperparts and upperwings, scaly pale fringes on the back and uppertail coverts, streaked whitish head, long narrow wings, short dark brown tail, head, body and tail in a straight line
adult in flight seen from below: white body and white underwing coverts bordered by dark flight feathers, pale streaked head, pale bill, short dark tail
adult resting on the sea, side view: white face and crown streaked dark brown, dark brown neck sides and scapulars, white throat and breast, long pale hooked bill
art.build: Large shearwater, about the length of a Black-tailed Gull but with much longer, narrower wings and a slimmer body. Head rounded, neck short. Bill long and slender, about as long as the head, with tube nostrils on top and a hooked tip. Legs short and set far back; on land it shuffles rather than standing upright. On the water it rests like a duck, the folded wings reaching about the tail tip. Tail short, rounded, dark. Flight: slow, loose wingbeats and long glides on slightly bowed wings.
avoid: Do not paint an all-dark brown bird (Sooty or Flesh-footed Shearwater); this species has white underparts and a streaked whitish head.
Do not paint a gull: no grey mantle, no white tail, and the bill is slim, hooked and tube-nosed.
Do not paint a dark bill; it is pale pinkish-horn with a darker tip.
Do not show it standing upright on long legs; its legs are short and set far back.
